To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) disadvantaged groups in natural resource governance interventions are not empowered to make their own choices and decisions; (2) the interventions are more about the empowerment of the local government and local elites; and (3) there is no clear and transparent process for the engagement of disadvantaged groups in natural resources governance.
disadvantaged groups are not sufficiently and meaningfully included in decision making on natural resources governance.
the formal possibilities do not provide citizens sufficient and equal space to engage meaningfully in the decision-making process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the engagement of the disadvantaged groups is facilitated by formal and informal mechanisms in natural resource governance.
the extent to which disadvantaged groups are empowered in natural resources governance.
how to move from blueprints to empowerment of disadvantaged groups in natural resource governance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the engagement of disadvantaged groups is not a matter of a single intervention but rather a long-term, continuous and inclusive process.
disadvantaged groups are included, but not empowered.
disadvantaged groups are included and empowered in natural resources governance only to a limited extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

empowerment is a necessary condition for the engagement of disadvantaged groups in natural resource governance, and the empowerment of disadvantaged groups should be a priority in the design of governance interventions.
the engagement of disadvantaged groups in natural resources governance has not yet been fully empowered, but is rather a process that is still in the blueprinting stage.
the engagement of disadvantaged groups in natural resource governance is not a simple matter, and that the formal possibilities do not provide citizens sufficient space for meaningful participation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the empowerment of disadvantaged groups requires the creation of a space for meaningful participation in natural resource governance.
the engagement of disadvantaged groups in the natural resources governance is a process that needs to be facilitated.
the empowerment of disadvantaged groups requires a more inclusive and democratic approach.
